Header: Colletotrichum capsici ( Colletotrichum truncatum ) Bangla name: Maricher khato/Foska

Prevention: Collect disease-free seeds from healthy plants.
Rotate chilli crop every 2 years with non-host crops (e.g. maize, sorghum and groundnuts).
Keep the land open to sunshine for 5-8 days before sowing
Monitoring: Disease appears mainly at mid-growth to maturity stage of crop
Symptoms may appear on leaf, stem and fruit
The symptoms first appear as small, water-soaked lesions on leaves that expand rapidly.
Lesions on fruits are usually round and sunken and may be over an inch in diameter depending on the size of the fruit.
Plant may die rapidly and disease may cause 50–100% yield loss.
High relative humidity (above 80%) and high temperature favour the disease.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy the heavily infected plants.
Collect and destroy the infected twigs and fruits.
Restrictions: Do not drink, eat or smoke during spraying
Wear mask, gloves, apron, gumboots, goggles, etc. while handling and spraying pesticides.
U, unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use; FRAC code 1.
